findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the MCP-server `reconcile` tool + its `mode` gating (mcp_server.py, _mcp_reads.py, scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py, docs/output-schemas.md) as consumers that the reconcile/`--mode` retirement must update, or scope them out explicitly.
evidence: mcp_server.py:5,8 documents a `reconcile` tool defaulting to dry-run; mcp_server.py:385-401 loads MODE_CAPS/Mode to gate modes
_mcp_reads.py:291 `if MODE_CAPS[parsed] != 0` — the MCP reconcile arm reads the mode cap table
scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py:45 registers a `reconcile` special-case row; docs/output-schemas.md and the generated MCP reference document it
Plan text names only `_cli/__init__.py:145-160` and `_lib_ops.py:92` as reconcile entry points and says 'three entry points' — the MCP tool is a fourth surface not listed
findings.finding: The plan removes `reconcile` and `--mode` but enumerates only the CLI wrapper (_cli/__init__.py:145-160); it does not enumerate the MCP-server `reconcile` tool and its `mode` argument as a consumer requiring update, though AC '--mode is gone from every surface' and 'reconcile ... removed' implicate it.
findings.location: Plan body (reconcile/--mode retirement) + AC '--mode is gone from every surface'
scenarios: An implementer removes reconcile from the CLI but leaves the MCP `reconcile` tool live, so `--mode`/`mode` survives on the MCP surface and AC '--mode is gone from every surface' fails
The generated MCP reference (gen_mcp_reference.py) still emits a `reconcile` row after retirement
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit line to the plan stating whether the MCP `reconcile` tool and its `mode` parameter are retired/renamed alongside the CLI, and list mcp_server.py / _mcp_reads.py / gen_mcp_reference.py / output-schemas.md as edit targets.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether the public library API `rebar.reconcile(mode=...)` (src/rebar/__init__.py + _lib_ops.py:92) and its `mode` parameter are retired/renamed by this plan, or explicitly out of scope.
evidence: src/rebar/__init__.py:49-52 `from rebar._lib_ops import (bridge_fsck, reconcile,)` — reconcile is public library API
_lib_ops.py:92 `def reconcile(mode: str = 'dry-run', ...)` with a `mode` param whose docstring lists reconcile-check|dry-run|bootstrap-*|live
README.md:496 documents `rebar.reconcile('dry-run')` as the library call
findings.finding: The plan does not enumerate the Python library public API `rebar.reconcile(mode=...)` (re-exported in __init__.py) as a consumer of the reconcile verb / `mode` concept it retires, even though it cites the same file (_lib_ops.py:92) only for the dry-run default.
scenarios: The CLI `reconcile` verb is removed but `rebar.reconcile(mode=...)` remains a public function taking the very `mode` string the plan says 'disappears entirely', leaving a mode surface on the library API

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion that exercises check-access end-to-end (creates then deletes a real/sandbox Jira issue and reports success), covering the setup final-validation call.
evidence: 'an operation that creates and deletes a real Jira issue'
'setup calls check-access as its final validation step'
No AC names check-access or setup verification
findings.finding: check-access 'creates and deletes a real Jira issue' and setup 'calls check-access as its final validation step' — a new live-external mutating path — yet no acceptance criterion exercises check-access (or setup) end-to-end against live Jira. AC1 only asserts the verb set 'exists'.
findings.location: 'check-access proves your access' / 'setup calls check-access as its final validation step'
scenarios: check-access ships but the create/delete round-trip is never exercised; a broken remote-write path passes CI on offline verb-existence checks alone.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify `bridge pause`/`bridge resume` against a current done-definition (name the pause mechanism/state they act on), or drop them until a consumer exists — pausing sync is currently an Actions-UI action, not a local CLI capability.
evidence: grep for `pause`/`resume` under src/rebar shows NO existing bridge pause/resume command (only workflow-run resume and llm checkpoint resume)
docs/jira-sync-setup.md:381-385 'Rollback / disable' documents pausing as 'disable Reconcile Bridge in the Actions UI (or delete its schedule: trigger)' — an operator/CI action, not a rebar verb
The plan's prose justifies only the three retirements and the --mode->preview/sync collapse; pause/resume appear ONLY in the verb-set line and are never tied to a current need or a backing mechanism
findings.finding: The plan introduces `bridge pause` and `bridge resume` as new verbs with no existing implementation and no stated current done-definition; today pausing sync is done by disabling the GitHub Actions workflow in the UI, not via a local CLI verb.
findings.location: Plan header verb set: 'rebar bridge setup | doctor/fsck | status | preview | sync | pause | resume'
scenarios: A reviewer/implementer asks what `bridge pause` mutates: there is no local pause state, and a local CLI cannot pause a scheduled GitHub workflow
Two new verbs ship with help text but no consumer, expanding the command surface ahead of demand

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Label each surviving flag as RETAINED/RENAMED vs NEWLY INTRODUCED (`--max-changes`, `--except`, `--max-age` have no current call-sites; `--only` today is fsck-only single-value) and tie each new flag to a current done-definition.
evidence: grep `--max-changes` → no matches; grep `--except` → no matches; grep `--max-age` → no matches
grep `--only` → exists only on fsck (src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:480-494) with a single value `stale-channel`, not a general id list
grep `--filter-local-ids` → the internal flag the plan says --only/--except replace (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:520)
'survive' framing implies pre-existing candidates; three of the four do not exist to 'survive'
findings.finding: The plan frames the surviving flags as 'Ten candidates reduced to FOUR' (implying all four pre-exist), but `--max-changes`, `--except`, and `--max-age` have zero existing call-sites; only `--only` (on fsck) and the internal `--filter-local-ids` they replace actually exist. New flags are not distinguished from retained ones, so the YAGNI screen cannot confirm each new flag serves a current done-definition.
findings.location: Plan section: 'Flags survive only if their help text can be written without internals. Ten candidates reduced to FOUR'
scenarios: An A1/YAGNI check treats --max-age and --except as existing survivors and skips validating that a current done-definition needs them
--only is repurposed from a single-value fsck repair selector into a general id filter without the plan noting the semantic change

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add acceptance criteria that exercise the new behavior end-to-end: a live/round-trip check-access including its failure path (missing/expired access, half-completed create/delete) and setup's handling of that failure, plus coverage that `--only`/`--except` actually narrow what is EXAMINED and that `bridge sync` mutates as specified.
evidence: 'check-access ... an operation that creates and deletes a real Jira issue'
'`--only`/`--except` limit what is EXAMINED as well as what is changed (unlike the internal `--filter-local-ids` they replace, which filtered only writes)'
ACs enumerate only structural/help-text/citation checks; none exercises sync mutation, the new examine-scoping semantics, or check-access against the remote incl. its failure path
findings.finding: The plan introduces new/changed user-facing behavior — default-mutating `bridge sync`, `--only`/`--except` that now widen scope to what is EXAMINED (a semantic change from the write-only `--filter-local-ids` they replace), and a `check-access` verb that creates and deletes a real Jira issue — but every acceptance criterion is a structural surface check (verb exists, help text wording, citation corrected). No test work is named for these flows, and in particular no failure/timeout/invalid-access path for the live-boundary `check-access` (and `setup`'s final validation that calls it).
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria; '`check-access` proves your access'; '`setup` calls `check-access` as its final validation step'
scenarios: check-access run when Jira credentials are missing/expired or the create-then-delete round-trip half-fails (issue created, delete errors) — no criterion proves the error is surfaced or the orphaned issue is handled
setup's final validation step fails at check-access — no criterion establishes what the user observes or that setup reports the failure

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the AC's bridge-verb count: `rebar --help` today lists FOUR bridge-prefixed verbs (purge-bridge, bridge-status, bridge-fsck, bridge-probe), not three — reconcile appearing zero times is accurate.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/help/overview.txt:27,29,30,31 list purge-bridge, bridge-status, bridge-fsck, bridge-probe — four bridge-prefixed entries, not three
The 'reconcile appears ZERO times' half of the same claim IS verified: search of overview.txt for 'reconcile' returns no matches
The 'one dead' refers to bridge-status, consistent with the rest of the plan
findings.finding: The AC line asserting current-state help output claims 'three bridge verbs (one dead) are listed' in rebar --help, but the actual overview help lists FOUR bridge-prefixed verbs: purge-bridge, bridge-status, bridge-fsck, bridge-probe. The count is a codebase assertion that a Read refutes.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, bullet: '`bridge` appears in `rebar --help`; today `reconcile` appears ZERO times while three bridge verbs (one dead) are listed'
scenarios: An implementer or verifier uses the AC's stated count to check the before-state and finds a mismatch, casting doubt on the AC
findings.suggested_fix: Change 'three bridge verbs (one dead) are listed' to 'four bridge-prefixed verbs (purge-bridge, bridge-status [dead], bridge-fsck, bridge-probe) are listed'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the canonical verb set explicit: list check-access in the verb enumeration and pick ONE name for the health verb (doctor vs fsck), used consistently in body and ACs.
evidence: 'rebar bridge setup | doctor/fsck | status | preview | sync | pause | resume'
'check-access is its own verb, not a flag on the health verb'
AC: 'rebar bridge <verb> exists with the agreed verb set'
findings.finding: The opening verb enumeration 'setup | doctor/fsck | status | preview | sync | pause | resume' omits check-access, but the body declares 'check-access is its own verb, not a flag'. The 'agreed verb set' referenced by AC1 is therefore ambiguous: is check-access in the set or not, and is the health verb named 'doctor', 'fsck', or both?
findings.location: Intro verb list vs. 'check-access is its own verb' paragraph
scenarios: An executor reads AC1 and does not know whether check-access must be shippable as a verb.
The health verb ships as 'doctor' while a script/doc expects 'fsck', or vice versa.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify (or reconsider) making `--only`/`--except` narrow what is EXAMINED: explain why the original post-filter (full unfiltered differ inputs, filter only writes) is safe to abandon, and specify how cross-scope dependency/convergence/invariant computation stays correct for in-scope tickets when their related tickets are outside the scope set.
evidence: `--filter-local-ids` help text at src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:519-527: 'all three differs run on their full unfiltered inputs (same code paths as production) but only mutations targeting these IDs (or their bound Jira keys) reach the applier. For validation use only.'

tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_reconcile_filter.py:3-7 documents the post-filter contract: 'All three differs still run on full inputs (same code paths). Only mutations targeting filtered IDs ... reach apply. Invariant checks and recover_pending_bindings are skipped.'
The plan gives a consistency rationale but no mechanism analysis of the pre-filter's effect on diff/convergence correctness for in-scope tickets whose relationships cross the scope boundary.
findings.finding: The maintainer decision that `--only`/`--except` should 'limit what is EXAMINED as well as what is changed' silently converts the replaced `--filter-local-ids` from a deliberate POST-filter (runs all three differs on full, unfiltered inputs, then filters only which mutations reach the applier) into a PRE-filter that narrows the differ input set. The plan states the consistency rationale (examined == changed) but does not reason about the correctness consequence the original design guarded: convergence, invariant checks, and cross-ticket dependency edges are computed against the full graph, so narrowing examination can change which mutations/diffs are computed for the IN-scope tickets (e.g. an edge to an out-of-scope ticket).
findings.location: Plan body: 'Maintainer decision: `--only`/`--except` limit what is EXAMINED as well as what is changed (unlike the internal `--filter-local-ids` they replace, which filtered only writes ...)'
scenarios: Operator runs `bridge sync --only T-1` where T-1 depends on out-of-scope T-2; a pre-filter that removes T-2 from examined inputs changes the dependency diff computed for T-1 versus the current post-filter behavior.
A convergence/invariant check that previously ran against the full graph now runs against a narrowed set, masking or fabricating a diff.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the accepted format for --max-age (e.g. Go-style '7d/24h') and the id list separator for --only/--except.
evidence: '--max-age <duration>'
'--only <ids>', '--except <ids>'
findings.finding: The surviving flag '--max-age <duration>' does not specify the duration format, and '--only <ids>'/'--except <ids>' do not specify the id format/separator. Executors must guess (e.g. '7d' vs seconds; comma vs space).
scenarios: Executor implements --max-age as an integer seconds while a doc/user expects '7d'.
--only accepts space-separated ids while users pass comma-separated.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify check-access failure handling: cleanup/rollback on partial success (delete-on-failure), timeout, and a surfaced error state if the round-trip cannot complete.
evidence: 'an operation that creates and deletes a real Jira issue'
No mention of what happens if delete fails or the call times out
findings.finding: check-access creates and then deletes a real Jira issue (an external write). The plan states no error/cleanup handling for the partial-failure case: if creation succeeds but deletion fails, an orphaned Jira issue leaks with no surfaced error or retry/cleanup path.
findings.location: 'creates and deletes a real Jira issue'
scenarios: Jira create succeeds, delete fails (network/permission) -> orphaned test issue accumulates on every setup run.
Jira is slow/down during check-access -> setup hangs or fails with an unhandled error.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the back-out/migration posture for the removed verbs (e.g. deprecation-warn one release, or an explicit note that the no-alias hard break is accepted and how to revert), not release notes alone.
evidence: 'Aliasing would be a silent behaviour change; anyone with reconcile in a script must re-read the line.'
Release notes named, but no migration window / deprecation-first step
findings.finding: Retiring reconcile/bridge-status/purge-bridge with no aliases is an explicitly justified breaking change, but the plan states no back-out/rollback path for consumers whose scripts break at cutover beyond 'release notes'.
findings.location: AC: 'reconcile, bridge-status, purge-bridge are removed, with release notes; no aliases'
scenarios: A CI script calling `rebar reconcile` breaks immediately on upgrade with only release notes as warning.
